name: Aphrodite
description: Greek goddess of love, beauty, desire, and pleasure. Associated with the sea, roses, and the planet Venus.

name: Ares
description: Greek god of war, courage, and conflict. Associated with strength, martial valor, and the planet Mars.

name: Hermes
description: Greek god of travelers, thieves, merchants, and messengers. Guide of souls to the underworld. Associated with communication and Mercury.

name: Hekate
description: Goddess of magic, witchcraft, the moon, crossroads, and the underworld. Keeper of keys and guardian of thresholds.

name: Persephone
description: Goddess of the underworld and spring. Her journey between worlds embodies themes of transformation, death, and renewal.

name: Apollo
description: God of the sun, music, poetry, prophecy, and healing. Patron of the arts and the oracle at Delphi.

name: Artemis
description: Goddess of the hunt, wilderness, and the moon. Protector of women, children, and wild creatures.

name: Athena
description: Goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, crafts, and civilization. Patron of Athens and emblem of just leadership.

name: Poseidon
description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Master of the deep waters and forces of nature.

name: Zeus
description: King of the Olympian gods, ruler of sky and thunder. Associated with authority, justice, and leadership.

name: Dionysus
description: God of wine, ecstasy, theater, and fertility. Embodies the liberating power of altered states and creative madness.

name: Hephaestus
description: God of the forge, fire, and craftsmanship. Master craftsman and maker of divine weapons and tools.

name: Demeter
description: Goddess of grain, harvest, and the fertile earth. Her grief at Persephone's abduction brings winter to the world.

name: Eros
description: Primordial god of love and desire. Embodiment of creative and erotic love that moves through all of existence.

name: Isis
description: Great Egyptian goddess of magic, healing, and motherhood. Powerful magician and devoted protector of the vulnerable.

name: Osiris
description: Egyptian god of the afterlife, resurrection, and agriculture. His story of death and rebirth embodies transformative cycles.

name: Thoth
description: Egyptian god of writing, knowledge, magic, and the moon. Keeper of sacred records and master of occult wisdom.

name: Anubis
description: Egyptian god of the dead and embalming. Guide of souls through the afterlife and guardian of tombs.

name: Ra
description: Egyptian sun god and king of the gods. His daily journey across the sky represents the triumph of light over darkness.

name: Bastet
description: Egyptian cat goddess of protection, joy, and the home. Associated with feminine power, sensuality, and guardian energy.

name: Sekhmet
description: Lioness goddess of war, fire, and healing. She embodies both destruction and the power to heal great wounds.

name: Hathor
description: Egyptian goddess of love, beauty, music, and motherhood. Embodies joy, abundance, and celestial love.

name: Ma'at
description: Egyptian goddess of truth, justice, and cosmic order. Her feather weighs against the heart of the deceased.

name: Nephthys
description: Egyptian goddess of death, night, and mourning. Sister of Isis and companion of the dead.

name: Odin
description: Allfather of the Norse gods. God of wisdom, war, poetry, and magic. Seeker of hidden knowledge at great personal cost.

name: Freyja
description: Norse goddess of love, beauty, war, and seidr magic. Leader of the Valkyries and keeper of the dead.

name: Thor
description: Norse god of thunder, strength, and protection of humanity. Wielder of Mjolnir, the divine hammer.

name: Loki
description: Norse trickster god of change and transformation. Shape-shifter who catalyzes necessary chaos and creative upheaval.

name: Frigg
description: Norse queen of the gods, goddess of marriage, motherhood, and foresight. Weaver of fate and keeper of hearth.

name: Tyr
description: Norse god of law, justice, and righteous combat. He sacrificed his hand to bind Fenrir for the good of all.

name: Baldur
description: Norse god of light, beauty, and purity. His death and eventual return symbolize the cycles of light and rebirth.

name: Hel
description: Norse ruler of the realm of the dead. Daughter of Loki who governs those who die of illness, old age, or natural causes.

name: The Morrígan
description: Irish triple goddess of fate, war, and sovereignty. Shapeshifter who appears as crow, wolf, and eel. Prophetess of battle outcomes.

name: Brigid
description: Irish goddess of healing, poetry, and the forge. Associated with Imbolc, her sacred flame is tended continuously.

name: Cernunnos
description: Celtic horned god of nature, wild animals, and the cycle of life. Master of the forest and the liminal spaces between worlds.

name: Lugh
description: Irish god of the sun, skill, and craftsmanship. Patron of all arts and the harvest festival of Lughnasadh.

name: Inanna
description: Sumerian goddess of love, war, justice, and political power. Her descent and return from the underworld is among humanity's oldest myths.

name: Kali
description: Hindu goddess of time, destruction, and liberation. Her fierce aspect dissolves ego and illusion, freeing the soul.

name: Lakshmi
description: Hindu goddess of wealth, fortune, and beauty. She embodies auspiciousness and is celebrated at Diwali.

name: Saraswati
description: Hindu goddess of knowledge, music, the arts, and wisdom. Patron of learning and eloquence.

name: Ganesha
description: Hindu elephant-headed deity of beginnings and removal of obstacles. Invoked at the start of any important undertaking.

name: Shiva
description: Hindu god of destruction and transformation. The destroyer of ego and illusion who makes way for new creation.

name: Durga
description: Hindu warrior goddess and protector. Her fierce power defeats demons and protects the righteous.

name: Archangel Raphael
description: Raphael, whose name means 'the healing of God,' is the archangel of air and the East. Associated with spring, intellect, logic, and reason. As archangel of Tiphareth on the Tree of Life, Raphael regulates and harmonizes the energies of all spheres, and is also correlated with victory, success, and prosperity.
attributes: Holds a caduceus (a staff with two entwined snakes)
Anything associated with spring (a damp, warm wind)
Golden robes and brilliant armor with the image of the sun on the breastplate (Tiphareth aspect)
reasonsToInvoke: To better articulate your ideas to others
For assistance with meditation and mental clarity
To enhance the intellect and learn deeper truths of philosophical and spiritual teachings
For all manner of healing—physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual
To repair rifts between yourself and others
To attain fame or popularity through talent
To pacify aggressive situations and gain victory over enemies
To improve physical vitality and stamina
For any sort of material prosperity

name: Archangel Gabriel
description: Gabriel is the archangel of water and the West, most associated with autumn, love, and the subconscious mind. Her domain is intuition, emotions, and dreams. As archangel of Yesod on the Tree of Life, Gabriel governs the astral plane, the moon, and the ebb and flow of etheric energy.
attributes: Anything associated with autumn (cool air, the smell of fallen leaves)
Purple robes and a silver headband with a crescent moon (Yesod aspect)
reasonsToInvoke: To heal any form of emotional wounding
For anything related to pure love
To increase the presence of love in your life
To bring peace and subdue aggression
To find answers in dreams and help interpret dreams
To gain insight on the workings of the astral realm
For emotional strength in times of crisis

name: Archangel Michael
description: Michael is the archangel of fire and the South, representing warrior energy associated with summer, courage, willpower, ambition, and sex drive. As archangel of Hod on the Tree of Life, Michael governs intellect, logic, travel, business, medicine, science, and magick—taking on a role of mediation and facilitation.
attributes: Anything associated with summer (heat, dryness, intense light)
Orange robes and a caduceus (Hod aspect)
reasonsToInvoke: To lose weight or get into shape
For any outcome associated with fire
To make intelligent decisions, especially during stressful times
For protection when performing magick (as well as to strengthen your magick)
For new business ideas and to meet with success in any business venture
To eloquently express yourself and your ideas

name: Archangel Uriel
description: Uriel is the archangel of earth and the North, associated with winter. He watches over and guides those who practice magick, especially with divination. His arena is the physical realm—particularly health, finances, and material wellbeing.
attributes: Holds a pentacle (a five-pointed star on a round disk)
Anything associated with winter (cold, crisp air; a frozen landscape; clear sky)
reasonsToInvoke: To obtain material goods and wealth

name: Archangel Metatron
description: Metatron is the only archangel said to have once been human—identified with the prophet Enoch, transformed by the divine into the angel closest to the throne of heaven. He directs the flow of purest divine energy down into denser levels of reality. As archangel of Kether, the crown of the Tree of Life, he represents complete union with the divine source. Invoking him raises one's energetic vibration toward enlightenment.
attributes: Stands or sits on a throne made of light
Robes of crystal clear light (Kether aspect)
reasonsToInvoke: To raise the vibrational frequency of a given area (a room, house, neighborhood, etc.)
To initiate the process of crossing the abyss
To complete the Great Work—to escape the wheel of samsara
To break free from the wheel of samsara, the endless cycle of suffering and rebirth
To align your individual will with the universal will
To see through the illusions of the material world
To raise the vibrational rate of your consciousness in order to display more aspects of divinity in your life

name: Archangel Sandalphon
description: Sandalphon regulates the flow of energy from divinity to the physical realm, gathering prayers and carrying them to the source of creation. Commander of the Ashim ('souls of fire') and archangel of music, fertility, and manifestation. Said to be the twin of Metatron and identified with the prophet Elijah. Presides over Malkuth on the Tree of Life—the densest level of reality where all physical things exist.
attributes: Holds a cornucopia (an overflowing basket of food)
reasonsToInvoke: To strengthen your powers of manifestation
To prevent financial or material loss
For greater strength and endurance, especially during adverse times
For assistance in creating music or to improve your musical ability
For assistance in working with plants
To spread a particular message in the world
To manifest anything in the material world
To bless your practical magick such that it manifests in a way that harms none

name: Archangel Kamael
description: Kamael, whose name means 'strength of God,' is the fiercest warrior among the celestial hosts. As archangel of Geburah on the Tree of Life, Kamael embodies strength, severity, courage, and self-discipline. He exists to protect those who cannot protect themselves, defending against strife swiftly and without remorse.
attributes: Red robes, crimson armor, and a helmet
reasonsToInvoke: To defeat enemies and defend against bullies
For bravery in the face of adversity
As a shield against aggressive people and situations
To project an aura of power
To express anger in a healthy way
To repel thieves and protect your home
For assistance in any type of competition

name: Archangel Haniel
description: Haniel presides over Netzach on the Tree of Life—the sphere of emotional life, art, beauty, sensuality, and luxury. Haniel possesses equally masculine and feminine energy, making this archangel receptive to any pronoun. Netzach is also the plane where the fey (faeries) exist—powerful entities with their own moral framework.
attributes: Accompanied by the scent of rose
reasonsToInvoke: To bring peace to arguing lovers
To encourage fidelity and enhance passion
To turn rivals and enemies into allies and friends
For assistance in creating any form of artwork
To create an environment in your home that is pleasing to all of the senses
To aid in gardening or any nature-related activities
To develop a mutually beneficial relationship with the fey

name: Archangel Tzadkiel
description: Tzadkiel is the archangel of Chesed on the Tree of Life, the sphere of abundance, prosperity, joy, and adventure. Said to have watched over Abraham, Tzadkiel is the archangel of luck—the more you work with him, the luckier you become. Associated with Jupiter energy, unconditional love, and devotion to the spiritual path. Burn bayberry and cedar to strengthen the connection.
attributes: Holds a scepter, like a king
reasonsToInvoke: For any form of prosperity and abundance
To attain inner harmony and joy
To enhance your popularity and the esteem of others
For the power to help others
To increase any talent or skill
To better understand your will and purpose in life
To make certain that others keep their promises

name: Archangel Tzaphkiel
description: Tzaphkiel is the archangel of Binah on the Tree of Life—the most feminine of all spheres, associated with Saturn, dark goddesses, karma, and old age. She helps us understand painful lessons necessary for spiritual development, teaching the value of silence. The principal work of Binah is the complete dissolution of the ego. Hers is not an energy to invoke lightly.
reasonsToInvoke: To bind enemies in order to prevent them from doing harm
To destroy the plans and schemes of enemies
To repel curses or other forms of negative energy
To bring justice upon those who have done you wrong
To project an aura of authority and gain the respect of others

name: Archangel Raziel
description: Raziel, the prince of hidden things, presides over Chokmah on the Tree of Life—the sphere of divine masculine energy where the distinction between creator and creation dissolves. Raziel causes epiphanies and realizations about magick and the universe, often through dreams, signs, and flashes of intuition. Said to witness and record everything on Earth in an infinitely enormous book that closes only when the last sentient being enters the divine realm.
reasonsToInvoke: To set plans in motion and speed up processes
To gain energy after you have been drained
To break free of any situation that feels like a rut
To obtain wisdom and deeper insight about any subject, especially anything pertaining to past civilizations and cultures
To discover forgotten or unrecorded magickal techniques

name: Bune
description: 26th spirit of the Goetia, a Duke appearing as a dragon with three heads (dog, griffin and man). Associated with wealth, eloquence, and communication with the departed.

name: Dantalion
description: 71st spirit of the Goetia. Depicted with many faces. Associated with knowledge of thoughts, influencing minds, and hidden wisdom.

name: Sallos
description: 19th spirit of the Goetia. Said to promote love between men and women and to bring peace between adversaries.

name: Marbas
description: 5th spirit of the Goetia. Associated with healing, knowledge of hidden things, and mechanical arts.

name: The Dark Knight Archetype
description: Archetypal figure of the wounded protector who channels grief and trauma into fierce justice and nocturnal vigilance.

name: The Jedi Archetype
description: Archetypal figure of the mindful warrior who balances the inner light and shadow. Embodies discipline, service, and the Force.

name: The Brilliant Witch Archetype
description: Archetypal figure of the studious magical practitioner who combines intellect, empathy, and fierce loyalty in service of good.

name: The Wise Mage Archetype
description: Archetypal figure of the ancient, wandering wizard who guides others through darkness toward their greatest potential.

name: Obatala
description: Orisha of purity, clarity, and creation. Father of all Orishas and molder of human bodies, associated with white, wisdom, and peaceful authority.

name: Yemaya
description: Orisha of the ocean and motherhood. Nurturing protector of women and children, governing the depths of the sea and the mysteries of life.

name: Shango
description: Orisha of thunder, lightning, and justice. Embodies fierce power, passion, and kingship. Patron of warriors and those who seek strength.

name: Ogun
description: Orisha of iron, labor, and war. Patron of blacksmiths, hunters, and warriors, governing all things made of iron and the clearing of obstacles.

name: Eshu
description: Orisha of crossroads, communication, and chance. Messenger between the divine and human realms, opener of paths and guardian of thresholds.

name: Oshun
description: Orisha of rivers, love, fertility, and prosperity. Embodiment of feminine sweetness, beauty, and abundance. Governs fresh water and matters of the heart.

name: Ifá
description: The sacred divination system and body of wisdom of Orunmila. Through its 256 odù (sacred verses), cast by trained babalawos and iyanifa, the Orishas communicate destiny and guidance to humanity.

name: Oya
description: Orisha of winds, storms, and transformation. Guardian of the cemetery and the passage between life and death, embodying radical change and fierce feminine power.

name: Orunmila
description: Orisha of knowledge, fate, and divination. Witness to all creation, Orunmila embodies the highest wisdom of the Ifá oracle and guides souls toward their destiny.

name: Ochosi
description: Orisha of the hunt, the forest, and justice. The divine tracker whose arrow never misses, one of the Warriors with Elegguá and Ogún, invoked by those seeking justice or facing the law.

name: Babalú-Ayé
description: Orisha of illness and healing, of smallpox and epidemics, and of those the world has cast aside. The humble father of the world who both brings disease and cures it.

name: Osain
description: Orisha of the forest and owner of every leaf, herb, and medicine. No ceremony can happen without his plants — "without leaves there is no Orisha." Depicted with one leg, one arm, and one eye.

name: Olokun
description: Orisha of the deepest ocean, where no light reaches. Keeper of sunken treasure, of the souls of the drowned, and of the vast wealth and mystery of the abyss.

name: Ibeji
description: The divine twins Taiwo and Kehinde — Orishas of childhood, joy, abundance, and good fortune. Sacred children who protect twins and all children, and whose laughter defeats even death.

name: Aganju
description: Orisha of volcanoes, the wilderness, and the raging river. A giant ferryman of immense strength, in Lucumí practice the father of Changó.

name: Oba
description: Orisha of marriage, devotion, and the Oba River. Changó's first wife, whose sacrifice of her own ear out of love makes her the patron of loyalty, and of those wounded by it.

name: Yewá
description: Orisha of purity, chastity, and the dead. The austere virgin who lives among the graves and delivers the bodies of the dead to Oyá. Served with the utmost modesty and silence.

name: J Dilla
description: Detroit beatmaker who revolutionized HipHop with unquantized drum programming and soulful sample manipulation. His album Donuts, completed while hospitalized, became a sacred text of underground music. Symbol of transcendence through craft and posthumous legacy.

name: Madlib
description: Prolific producer, rapper, and crate-digger whose alter ego Quasimoto channels psychedelic consciousness through HipHop. His Beat Konducta series and collaborations with MF DOOM and J Dilla explore the outer dimensions of sound and culture.

name: Tyler, the Creator
description: Odd Future founder and genre-defying artist who evolved from provocateur to visionary producer-vocalist. His albums Flower Boy, Igor, and Call Me If You Get Lost trace an arc of self-discovery, emotional vulnerability, and maximalist artistic freedom.

name: Nipsey Hussle
description: Crenshaw rapper and community activist who embodied the Marathon Consciousness—a philosophy of self-reliance, long-term vision, and investment in one's community. Posthumously recognized as a symbol of Black entrepreneurship and spiritual legacy.

name: Myka 9
description: Los Angeles lyricist and Freestyle Fellowship member whose rapid-fire delivery and jazz-influenced flows expanded the boundaries of conscious rap. A practitioner of the verbal arts as a form of higher consciousness and community healing.

name: Sole
description: Anti-capitalist rapper and spoken word artist whose DIY ethos and unflinching political critique challenge systems of oppression. Founder of Anticon Records and practitioner of HipHop as radical social magic.

name: MF DOOM
description: The masked villain rapper who constructed an elaborate mythology of villainy, wordplay, and hidden identity. His intricate internal rhymes, comic-book references, and mask persona made him an archetypal trickster-mage of HipHop. Operation Doomsday and Madvillainy are his grimoires.

name: Rick Ross
description: Miami rapper and Maybach Music Group founder who embodies the Boss archetype—a figure of abundance, luxury, and commanding presence. His baroque production style and larger-than-life persona invoke the Jupiterian energy of expansion and material mastery.

name: Erykah Badu
description: Neo-soul queen and afrofuturist priestess whose music channels ancestral memory, cosmic consciousness, and feminine spiritual power. Her Baduizm and Mama's Gun albums initiated a generation into soul music as sacred practice and metaphysical inquiry.

name: Saul Williams
description: Poet, rapper, and actor who bridges spoken word, HipHop, and industrial music. His work channels Afronautics and radical consciousness, using language as a weapon of liberation. Slam (1998) brought spoken word to mainstream consciousness.

name: DJ QBert
description: San Francisco-based turntablist widely considered one of the greatest scratch DJs in history. His Invisibl Skratch Piklz crew pioneered scratch music as a spiritual and martial art, transmuting vinyl into a vehicle of cosmic sound manipulation.

name: Lauryn Hill
description: Fugees member whose debut solo album The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill fused rap, R&B, and reggae with spiritual awakening and Womanist theology. An archetypal figure of sacred feminine power, redemption, and the courage to speak prophetic truth.

name: Jay Electronica
description: New Orleans-born rapper whose rare recordings and mystical persona cultivated an esoteric legend. A student of the Five-Percent Nation and later the Nation of Islam, his lyricism weaves sacred geometry, divine mathematics, and urban prophecy into HipHop.

name: Tupac Shakur
description: Poet-warrior and cultural martyr whose music addressed police brutality, poverty, and spiritual longing with equal passion. THUG LIFE (The Hate U Give Little Infants F***s Everybody) encodes a philosophy of systemic critique. His posthumous influence is a testament to art as immortality.

name: Chuck D
description: Public Enemy co-founder and architect of HipHop as political warfare. His booming baritone and Bomb Squad production created sonic monuments of Black resistance. Fight the Power and It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back are manifestos disguised as music.

name: Flavor Flav
description: Public Enemy hype man and court jester who wears a giant clock as a talisman of time consciousness. His chaotic energy balances Chuck D's gravity, embodying the trickster principle—the sacred fool who disrupts order to reveal deeper truths.

name: Kendrick Lamar
description: Compton rapper and Pulitzer Prize winner whose albums To Pimp a Butterfly and DAMN. explore Black identity, trauma, prophetic calling, and spiritual wrestling with God. His work is revered as scripture by a generation seeking meaning in sound.

name: E-40
description: Bay Area rap legend and vernacular innovator who coined hundreds of slang terms now embedded in American English. His linguistic creativity, entrepreneurial hustle, and decades-spanning catalog make him a trickster-merchant of language magic.

name: Rammellzee
description: Bronx-born artist, rapper, and theorist who developed Gothic Futurism and Ikonoklast Panzerism—a philosophy of letter and language as cosmic warfare. His armor sculptures and esoteric rap texts bridge graffiti, HipHop, and hermetic magic into a unified system of symbolic combat.

name: KRS-One
description: The Teacha and Boogie Down Productions founder who declared HipHop a religion and philosophy, not a genre. His Gospel of Hip Hop codified the nine elements of HipHop culture. A living archetype of the rapper as griot, philosopher, and spiritual warrior.

name: Kanye West
description: Chicago producer-rapper whose career arc from College Dropout to Donda traces themes of ego, hubris, divine calling, and breakdown. A maximalist artist whose creative megalomania and gospel-influenced production channel the archetype of the inspired genius at war with limitation.

name: Rick Rubin
description: Legendary producer and minimalist mystic who approaches music as sacred space creation. Co-founded Def Jam and produced landmark albums across genres through the art of reduction and deep listening. Embodies the Hermit archetype—stripping away excess to reveal essence, creating transformative containers through silence, presence, and witness consciousness.

name: Frida Kahlo
description: Mexican painter who turned lifelong pain — polio as a child, a near-fatal bus accident at eighteen — into unflinching self-portraits, many painted from a mirror fixed above her bed. The archetype of the wounded artist who makes her own body the altar.
reasonsToInvoke: Claiming your own image and identity
Courage to be seen as you are

name: Jean-Michel Basquiat
description: Brooklyn-born painter who went from the SAMO© graffiti of lower Manhattan to international acclaim before his death at twenty-seven. His crowned, word-crossed canvases confront race, power and history. The archetype of the self-crowned genius burning fast and bright.

name: Vincent van Gogh
description: Dutch painter who made some 860 oil paintings in a decade, most in his last two years, and sold almost nothing in his lifetime. His letters to his brother Theo record a devotion to light, color and humble things. The archetype of the ardent visionary misunderstood in his own time.
reasonsToInvoke: Devotion to your craft through obscurity

name: Nina Simone
description: Classically trained pianist from Tryon, North Carolina, who fused Bach with jazz, blues and gospel and turned her voice on the civil rights struggle. “I'll tell you what freedom is to me: no fear.” The archetype of the uncompromising artist whose art is her protest.
reasonsToInvoke: Courage to speak out through art

name: Prince
description: Minneapolis multi-instrumentalist who wrote, produced and played much of his own music across funk, rock, pop and gospel, and fought for ownership of his work — changing his name to an unpronounceable symbol in 1993. The archetype of the androgynous, prolific creative sovereign.
aliases: The Artist Formerly Known as Prince

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: German philosopher who proclaimed the death of God, the will to power and the eternal return, and asked how life can be affirmed without borrowed values; he thought much of his work out walking the Alps around Sils-Maria. The archetype of the iconoclast who breaks idols to make room for new values.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
description: French existentialist philosopher and novelist whose The Second Sex argued that “one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.” She wrote at the café tables of Saint-Germain-des-Prés. The archetype of the free woman who makes her own ethics.
reasonsToInvoke: Becoming who you choose to be

name: Albert Camus
description: French-Algerian writer and Nobel laureate who faced the absurd — a world silent to our longing for meaning — and answered with revolt, freedom and passion rather than despair. “One must imagine Sisyphus happy.” The archetype of the rebel who finds an invincible summer within.

name: Hannah Arendt
description: German-American political theorist who fled Nazi Germany and wrote on totalitarianism, action and responsibility; reporting on the Eichmann trial, she named “the banality of evil.” She called her method “thinking without a banister.” The archetype of the independent mind that judges for itself.

name: Alan Watts
description: British-born interpreter of Zen, Taoism and Vedanta whose radio talks and books made Eastern thought playful and plain for the West. He lived on the ferryboat Vallejo in Sausalito and died at Druid Heights on Mount Tamalpais. The archetype of the laughing mystic.

name: Nikola Tesla
description: Serbian-American inventor who pioneered alternating-current power, the induction motor and the Tesla coil, and dreamed of wireless energy for the world at Wardenclyffe. He died alone in room 3327 of the Hotel New Yorker. The archetype of the solitary visionary ahead of his time.
reasonsToInvoke: Persisting when you are ahead of your time

name: Marie Curie
description: Polish-French physicist and chemist who, with Pierre Curie, discovered polonium and radium in a leaking shed in Paris, and coined the word “radioactivity.” The first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences. The archetype of the tireless pioneer who illuminates the unseen.
reasonsToInvoke: Courage in a field that shuts you out

name: Albert Einstein
description: German-born physicist who, as a patent clerk in Bern, published in 1905 the papers on light quanta, Brownian motion and special relativity, and in 1915 completed general relativity. He held imagination more important than knowledge. The archetype of the playful genius who thinks in pictures.

name: Carl Sagan
description: American astronomer who helped design the Pioneer plaque and the Voyager Golden Record, persuaded NASA to turn Voyager 1's camera back for the Pale Blue Dot, and carried the cosmos to millions through television. The archetype of wonder joined to skepticism.

name: Rosalind Franklin
description: English chemist whose X-ray diffraction image, Photo 51, revealed the helical structure of DNA; it was shown to Watson and Crick without her knowledge. She went on to map the structure of viruses. The archetype of exacting brilliance too long overlooked.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
description: Baptist minister who led the American civil rights movement through nonviolent resistance — Montgomery, Birmingham, Selma — and dreamed aloud at the Lincoln Memorial in 1963. Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964; assassinated in 1968. The archetype of the prophetic dreamer of justice.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
description: Indian lawyer who led India's independence movement through satyagraha — truth-force, nonviolent mass resistance — from the Salt March to spinning his own cloth. The archetype of the ascetic who moves empires by self-discipline.

name: Nelson Mandela
description: South African anti-apartheid leader imprisoned for twenty-seven years, eighteen of them on Robben Island, who emerged to negotiate the end of apartheid and became his country's first democratically elected president. The archetype of endurance transfigured into reconciliation.

name: Malcolm X
description: Self-educated in a prison library, he became the most incisive voice of Black self-determination in 1960s America; after his pilgrimage to Mecca he broadened his vision toward universal human rights. Assassinated at the Audubon Ballroom in 1965. The archetype of radical self-transformation.

name: Eleanor Roosevelt
description: First Lady who remade the role into a platform for social justice, wrote the “My Day” column for more than a quarter-century, and chaired the UN commission that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. “You must do the thing you think you cannot do.” The archetype of compassion turned into tireless public work.
reasonsToInvoke: Courage to do what you think you cannot

name: Maya Angelou
description: Poet, memoirist and performer who wrote of surviving trauma and silence in I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, and read “On the Pulse of Morning” at the 1993 presidential inauguration. She wrote in rented hotel rooms with a Bible, a thesaurus, a deck of cards and a bottle of sherry. The archetype of the voice that rises.

name: James Baldwin
description: Harlem-born novelist and essayist who wrote about race, sexuality and love with prophetic clarity, much of it from abroad in France. The archetype of the witness who tells the truth with love.

name: Octavia E. Butler
description: Science-fiction writer from Pasadena whose novels of power, survival and adaptation — and the Earthseed verses of the Parable books, “God is Change” — now read as prophecy. The first science-fiction writer awarded a MacArthur Fellowship. The archetype of the visionary who writes the future into being.

name: Franz Kafka
description: Prague insurance official who wrote by night of transformation, guilt and labyrinthine authority, and asked that his manuscripts be burned; his friend Max Brod published them instead. The archetype of the anxious dreamer who maps the absurd.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
description: Colombian novelist and journalist whose magical realism, born of his grandmother's deadpan storytelling in Aracataca, created the town of Macondo; awarded the Nobel Prize in 1982. The archetype of the storyteller for whom the marvelous is everyday.

name: Bruce Lee
description: San Francisco–born, Hong Kong–raised martial artist, actor and philosopher who founded Jeet Kune Do, “the style of no style,” and broke Hollywood's barriers for Asian actors. The archetype of disciplined fluidity: “Be water, my friend.”

name: Muhammad Ali
description: Three-time heavyweight champion who floated like a butterfly and stung like a bee, refused the Vietnam draft on principle at the cost of his title, and turned boasting into poetry. The archetype of the Greatest — brash, joyful and unbowed.

name: Bob Marley
description: Jamaican singer-songwriter who carried reggae and the Rastafari message of redemption and One Love to the world, and in 1978 brought two rival political leaders together on stage at the One Love Peace Concert. The archetype of the spiritual rebel who unites.

name: Amelia Earhart
description: Aviator who in 1932 became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic, and vanished over the Pacific in 1937 while attempting to circle the globe. The archetype of daring independence and the open horizon.

name: Steve Jobs
description: Co-founder of Apple who, from his parents' garage in Los Altos, helped bring the personal computer, the Macintosh, Pixar's films, the iPod and the iPhone to the world, driven by an obsession with simplicity and design. The archetype of the perfectionist visionary.

name: Rat
description: The first of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac — earthly branch 子 (zǐ), yang Water, the animal of midwinter and of the hours 11 pm – 1 am. Traditionally quick-witted, resourceful and charming.
reasonsToInvoke: Drawing on the Rat’s quick-witted and resourceful nature

name: Wolf
description: The wild hunter of the pack: companion of Odin, nurse of Rome's founders, and in Rome the sacred animal of Mars.

name: Hound
description: The guardian and guide at the threshold: Hecate's hounds at the crossroads, Cerberus at the gate of Hades, jackal-headed Anubis leading the dead.

name: Fox
description: The clever trickster who slips every trap: Inari's messenger in Japan, the uncatchable Teumessian fox of Greek myth, Reynard of medieval fable.

name: Bear
description: The great protector who sleeps through winter and wakes renewed: Artemis's 'little bears' at Brauron, Callisto in the stars, the Norse berserkers' fury.

name: Stag
description: The antlered lord of the forest, whose crown falls and grows again each year: Cernunnos, Artemis's hind, the stag on Valhalla's roof.

name: Boar
description: The fearless charger with the golden bristles: Freyr's mount, Vishnu's avatar who raised the earth, the crest of Celtic and Anglo-Saxon warriors.

name: Lion
description: The king of beasts and the Sun's own animal: Sekhmet the Eye of Ra, the Nemean lion's hide on Heracles, Ishtar's lions on Babylon's Processional Way, Durga's mount.

name: Bull
description: The strength and fertility of the earth: Apis of Memphis, Nandi at Shiva's door, the Bull of Heaven, Taurus ruled by Venus.

name: Cat
description: The independent night-watcher whose eyes follow the Moon: Bastet of Bubastis, and the pair of cats that draw Freyja's chariot.

name: Raven
description: The black messenger of thought and memory: Odin's Huginn and Muninn, Apollo's bird, the Morrígan's form over the battlefield.

name: Owl
description: The silent seer of the night: Athena's little owl on the coins of Athens, the owl of Minerva that flies at dusk.

name: Eagle
description: The sovereign of the sky, bearer of Jupiter's thunderbolts: the eagle atop Yggdrasil, the standard of Rome's legions, the emblem of St John.

name: Falcon
description: The swift, far-seeing bird of the rising Sun: Horus of the sky and of kingship, Ra-Horakhty, and Freyja's falcon-feather cloak.

name: Swan
description: The graceful shape-changer: Apollo's swans, Zeus coming to Leda, the Children of Lir, and the hamsa of Saraswati.

name: Dove
description: The bird of love and of peace: Aphrodite's doves, Ishtar's bird, the dove with the olive leaf, the Spirit descending.

name: Ibis
description: The bird of Thoth, god of writing, wisdom and reckoning — the Hermes of the Egyptians.

name: Serpent
description: The ancient power that sheds its skin and is renewed: the rod of Asclepius, the uraeus of the pharaohs, the Ouroboros, the world-serpent.

name: Scarab
description: The sacred beetle that rolls the Sun into the sky each dawn: Khepri, 'he who comes into being.'

name: Bee
description: The tireless maker of honey and of community: born from the Sun god's tears in Egyptian myth, the 'Delphic Bee' of the oracle, the Melissae who served the goddess.
